title: The United States Faces Risk of Losing Measles-Free Status
subtitle: Health officials warn that a drop in vaccination rates is fueling the worst outbreak in over three decades.

summary.en: The United States is on the verge of losing its official measles-free status due to a major national outbreak. This development follows a significant decline in the percentage of the population receiving the measles vaccine. Experts warn that the disease is now spreading within communities across the country. Public health officials are urging citizens to locate their vaccination records to prepare for potential exposure. The situation marks a serious setback for public health efforts in the United States.
summary.zh: 由於全國性的大規模疫情，美國正處於失去官方「無麻疹國家」地位的邊緣。此發展源於人口疫苗接種率的顯著下降。專家警告，該疾病目前正在全國各社區內傳播。公共衛生官員呼籲民眾找出疫苗接種紀錄，以應對潛在的接觸風險。此情況標誌著美國公共衛生工作遭遇了嚴重的挫折。

paragraphs.en: The United States is currently facing a critical moment in public health as it nears the loss of its official measles-free status. This designation, which confirms that the virus is no longer constantly spreading in the country, could be removed as early as this week. According to The Guardian Health, this potential change comes during the worst measles outbreak the nation has seen in 35 years, with more than 5,400 cases reported across the country.
paragraphs.zh: 美國目前正處於公共衛生的關鍵時刻，即將失去官方認定的「無麻疹國家」地位。這項認證確認了該病毒已不再於國內持續傳播，但最快可能在本週被撤銷。根據《衛報健康版》（The Guardian Health）報導，這項潛在的變動發生在該國三十五年來最嚴重的麻疹疫情期間，全國已通報超過五千四百起病例。

paragraphs.en: If the United States loses this status, it will join several other nations that previously eliminated the disease only to see it return. A panel of eight independent experts from the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), a branch of the World Health Organization, is currently reviewing the evidence to make a final decision. Dr. Paul Offit, director of the Vaccine Education Center at the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia, told The Guardian Health that the virus now has a permanent foothold in the country. He noted that the situation is a "tremendous step backwards" caused by a significant decrease in the percentage of people getting vaccinated.
paragraphs.zh: 如果美國失去這項地位，將會加入其他幾個曾經根除該疾病卻又復發的國家行列。一個由泛美衛生組織（PAHO，世界衛生組織的分支機構）組成的八人獨立專家小組，目前正在審查相關證據以做出最終決定。費城兒童醫院疫苗教育中心主任保羅·奧菲特（Paul Offit）博士向《衛報健康版》表示，該病毒現在已在美國站穩腳跟。他指出，這是由於疫苗接種率顯著下降所導致的「巨大倒退」。

paragraphs.en: Measles is known as one of the most infectious diseases in medicine. While the majority of Americans still choose to vaccinate themselves and their children, the virus is so contagious that even small drops in immunity allow it to spread rapidly. The current outbreak has already had tragic consequences. The Guardian Health reports that six people have died in Pennsylvania this year, while other deaths have been recorded in New York and Wisconsin. Nearly every state in the country is currently dealing with an active outbreak.
paragraphs.zh: 麻疹被認為是醫學上最具傳染性的疾病之一。儘管大多數美國人仍選擇為自己和孩子接種疫苗，但該病毒傳染力極強，即使免疫人口比例出現微小下降，也足以讓病毒迅速擴散。目前的疫情已造成悲劇性後果。《衛報健康版》報導，今年賓州已有六人死亡，紐約州與威斯康辛州也出現死亡案例。目前美國幾乎每個州都在應對活躍的疫情。

paragraphs.en: This health crisis is changing the way officials approach daily life. Dr. David Margolius, the public health director in Cleveland, Ohio, is now advising people to find their proof of vaccination. He explained to The Guardian Health that this is necessary because people may be exposed to the virus in public spaces like hospital waiting rooms or elevators. Without proof of vaccination, individuals who are exposed to a patient with measles may face a 21-day quarantine—a period of time where a person stays away from others to prevent the spread of a disease. For many, this has become a stressful and unexpected part of their daily routine.
paragraphs.zh: 這場健康危機正在改變官員處理日常生活的方式。俄亥俄州克里夫蘭市的公共衛生局長大衛·馬戈利斯（David Margolius）博士，目前建議民眾找出自己的疫苗接種證明。他向《衛報健康版》解釋，這是必要的，因為人們可能會在醫院候診室或電梯等公共場所接觸到病毒。若無法提供接種證明，接觸過麻疹患者的人可能面臨二十一天的隔離——即為了防止疾病傳播而與他人保持距離的期間。對許多人來說，這已成為日常生活中充滿壓力且意想不到的一部分。

paragraphs.en: Experts are also observing a shift in who is catching the disease. Historically, measles was considered a childhood illness, with most people catching it before the age of five. However, the current data shows a different pattern. According to The Guardian Health, two-thirds of those infected in Pennsylvania are adults. Researchers are still working to understand this shift, as they have less information about how the virus affects this age group. There have even been cases where mothers have given birth to babies who already had the measles.
paragraphs.zh: 專家也觀察到感染族群的轉變。過去，麻疹被視為兒童疾病，大多數人在五歲前就會感染。然而，目前的數據顯示出不同的模式。根據《衛報健康版》報導，賓州感染者中有三分之二是成年人。研究人員仍在努力理解這種轉變，因為他們對於該病毒如何影響此年齡層的資訊較少。甚至出現了母親生下時就已患有麻疹的嬰兒案例。

paragraphs.en: Public health experts emphasize that the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine remains highly effective. Two doses of the vaccine provide 97% protection against the disease. Despite this, the combination of lower vaccination rates and the high contagiousness of the virus has created a difficult environment. As the country waits for the official decision from health authorities, the focus remains on tracking the virus and encouraging more people to get vaccinated to stop the spread.
paragraphs.zh: 公共衛生專家強調，麻疹、腮腺炎與德國麻疹混合疫苗（MMR）依然非常有效。接種兩劑疫苗可提供百分之九十七的保護力。儘管如此，疫苗接種率下降與病毒的高傳染性相結合，創造了一個艱困的環境。在等待衛生當局做出正式決定的同時，重點仍放在追蹤病毒，並鼓勵更多人接種疫苗以遏止擴散。

paragraphs.en: For many Americans, the threat of measles is a new experience. As Dr. Margolius noted, most people have no personal history with the disease, as it was previously rare in the United States. Now, health departments are doing a large amount of detective work to identify and reach out to anyone who may have been near an infected person. This ongoing effort highlights the challenges of managing a disease that was once thought to be under control. As the situation develops, health officials continue to stress that vaccination is the most important tool for protecting the public and regaining the country's measles-free status.
paragraphs.zh: 對許多美國人而言，麻疹的威脅是一種全新的體驗。正如馬戈利斯博士所言，大多數人對這種疾病沒有個人經驗，因為它過去在美國相當罕見。現在，衛生部門正進行大量的偵查工作，以識別並聯繫任何可能曾靠近感染者的人。這項持續的努力凸顯了管理一種曾被認為已受控制的疾病所面臨的挑戰。隨著局勢發展，衛生官員持續強調，疫苗接種是保護公眾並重獲無麻疹國家地位最重要的工具。

keyTerms.definitionEn: A secure position from which further progress can be made; here, it means the virus has established a permanent presence.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 立足點；在此指病毒已在該國紮根、長期存在。
keyTerms.noteZh: 原意指攀岩時腳踩的支撐點，這裡用來比喻病毒的擴散。文中：Dr. Paul Offit, director of the Vaccine Education Center at the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia, told The Guardian Health that the virus now has a permanent foothold in the country.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Small decreases or reductions in a level or amount.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作動詞（掉落），這裡作名詞使用，指免疫力水平的下降。文中：While the majority of Americans still choose to vaccinate themselves and their children, the virus is so contagious that even small drops in immunity allow it to spread rapidly.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To contact someone, often for help, information, or to provide support.
keyTerms.noteZh: 這是一個常見的片語，但在這裡指衛生部門主動聯繫可能接觸過病毒的人，而非字面上的「伸手」。文中：Now, health departments are doing a large amount of detective work to identify and reach out to anyone who may have been near an infected person.

quiz.question: What is the primary reason for the potential loss of the United States' measles-free status?

options.A: The virus has mutated into a more dangerous strain.
options.B: A decline in the percentage of the population receiving vaccinations.
options.C: The failure of the MMR vaccine to provide long-term protection.
options.D: A lack of coordination between state health departments.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第二段，Dr. Paul Offit 明確指出目前的困境是「疫苗接種率顯著下降」所導致的倒退。選項 A 文章未提及病毒變異；選項 C 與文章第六段矛盾，該段強調 MMR 疫苗仍有 97% 的保護力；選項 D 雖然提到各州都在處理疫情，但並非導致失去地位的根本原因。

quiz.question: Based on the information provided, what can be inferred about the current measles outbreak compared to historical patterns?

options.A: It is primarily affecting children under the age of five.
options.B: It is less contagious than outbreaks from 35 years ago.
options.C: It is affecting a wider age range of the population than in the past.
options.D: It is easier for health officials to track than previous outbreaks.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。第五段指出，過去麻疹被視為兒童疾病（五歲以下），但目前的數據顯示三分之二的感染者是成人，這顯示感染年齡層已發生轉變。選項 A 與文章敘述相反；選項 B 文章提到麻疹具有高度傳染性，並未暗示傳染力下降；選項 D 文章第七段提到官員需要進行大量的「偵探工作」，顯示追蹤過程相當困難，而非容易。

quiz.question: In the second paragraph, what does the phrase 'a permanent foothold' most closely mean?

options.C: A medical treatment for a virus.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在文中 'the virus now has a permanent foothold' 指的是病毒在美國已經「站穩腳跟」，即已經長期存在且難以根除。選項 B 與傷口無關；選項 C 錯誤理解了詞彙的隱喻；選項 D 的「短暫」與 'permanent'（永久的）意思完全相反。

quiz.question: What is the central message of the article?

options.A: The United States has successfully eradicated measles through new medical technology.
options.B: Measles is no longer a threat to the health of the American adult population.
options.C: The U.S. is facing a serious health crisis due to falling vaccination rates and the resurgence of measles.
options.D: Mandatory 21-day quarantines are the most effective way to eliminate the measles virus.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。整篇文章圍繞著美國即將失去「無麻疹國家」地位的危機，並分析了原因（疫苗接種率下降）、現狀（疫情擴散至成人）及應對措施（追蹤與接種）。選項 A 與事實相反；選項 B 忽略了成人感染比例高的事實；選項 D 僅是防疫措施之一，並非文章的核心主旨。
